 Tactically flexible Lampard wants to 'give ourselves a chance' published at 19:18 GMT 19:18 GMT 
 Everton v Coventry (20:00 GMT) 
 Nick Mashiter 
BBC Sport football news reporter 
 Despite Coventry's start to the season - after defeats by Arsenal, Hull, Manchester City and Brighton - the optimism at the training ground did not waver.
 The positive mood at the club's Ryton base remains, following Saturday's victory over Sunderland, as it did after the 5-0 home thumping by Brighton.
 It was accepted the game, where Coventry played almost 45 minutes with 10 men following Taiwo Awoniyi's dismissal, can happen in the Premier League - and there was no hangover.
 There was a belief there was enough evidence in performances against Hull, Manchester City and Arsenal the Sky Blues could compete in the top flight.
 Then, after a 3-1 Carabao Cup defeat by Aston Villa, Frank Lampard tweaked the system to match Nottingham Forest's back three to earn a 1-0 win at the City Ground.
 "The result sometimes you can't quite control, but you can control your idea going into a game, that maximises our strengths and looks at the opposition's," said Lampard, who is in before 7.30am every morning, using the gym before training.
 "There can be various reasons why we do it. We went to Nottingham Forest and we matched up their formation because I wasn't keen to go there in the moment we were in with a back four and the problems they can give you with wing-backs and 10s.
 "It's not just my, or our, choice on formation which is going to win or lose games. We know we have a big fight so every small percentage in our set-up if we feel that way we will do it - but we must feel it's going to be the right one."
 Lampard has always been tactically flexible and three wins in five games has allowed Coventry to climb out of the relegation zone.
 The stats provide interesting reading too, especially when compared with the 1-0 defeat by Hull which could have been so damaging in the first home game of the season.
 Then, Coventry had 68.5% possession but that dropped to 42.6% in the 3-1 win over Sunderland. The Sky Blues also made more than 200 fewer passes and more than 50 fewer forward passes against the Black Cats.
 Their passes in the final third more than halved from 128 to just 60, as the patience - and even pragmatism - paid off as the Sky Blues begin to understand the demands of the division.
 The benching of skipper Matt Grimes, key in last season's promotion, was also a big call from Lampard but one which has been met with understanding from within.
 Coventry still have the lowest xG (expected goals) in the Premier League of 8.34 but lessons have been learned from the frustration of the opening weeks, even if those at the club recognise the difficult start given three of their opening four away games were at Manchester City, Arsenal and Tottenham.
 After Everton, Coventry host Crystal Palace and Ipswich either side of a trip to Leeds to complete a run sources felt would be crucial to their survival hopes.
 "When you're in the zone, enjoyment of the win is pretty short-lived - you switch your attention to the next game. Relaxation and complacency is the biggest danger in this game," said Lampard.
 "If we can keep the strength of feeling, even when difficult results come, we will give ourselves a chance."

 Moyes equals Everton record published at 19:03 GMT 19:03 GMT 
 Everton v Coventry (20:00 GMT) 
 Nick Mashiter 
BBC Sport football news reporter at the Hill Dickinson Stadium 
 David Moyes is taking charge of his 592nd games as Everton manager - equalling Harry Catterick's record for the Toffees.
 Catterick - a centre-forward who also played for the club - won two First Division titles and the 1966 FA Cup with Everton and, like Moyes, managed Preston as well.
 "Tonight I am fully aware I equal Harry Catterick’s record of most matches as Everton manager," writes Moyes in the programme.
 "I am incredibly thrilled and honoured to have been given the opportunity to manage this football club in so many matches and for so many years. 
 "Seeing my name alongside Harry Catterick’s is hugely humbling and I hope I can continue to add to that figure. 
 "What I really hope, though, is that I can bring trophies to the club like Harry Catterick did in his period as Everton manager."

 Post published at 18:59 GMT 18:59 GMT 
 Everton v Coventry (20:00 GMT) 
 Matthew Hobbs 
BBC Sport journalist 
 Coventry failed to score as they lost their opening four matches on their return to the Premier League but they have since won three of the past five, including a 3-1 victory over Sunderland last time out.
 Lampard's side have been far more clinical in front of goal in those five matches, scoring nine times from an expected goals tally of just 4.12.
 It is the biggest overperformance of xG by any Premier League team over the five-game period.
 Everton and Coventry have not faced each other since 2001 but Lampard is likely to get a warm reception on Merseyside having steered the Toffees away from the threat of relegation in 2021-22 with a win in their penultimate match of that campaign against Crystal Palace.
 In the opposition dugout, Moyes will celebrate equalling Harry Catterick's club record of 592 games at the helm in a first appearance against Coventry – the 45th side he has faced in his Premier League career.

 Post published at 18:56 GMT 18:56 GMT 
 Everton v Coventry (20:00 GMT) 
 Matthew Hobbs 
BBC Sport journalist 
 Everton will attempt to win a third game in the space of just 10 days when they host former Toffees boss Frank Lampard and his Coventry side on Friday.
 The two victories over the past week – against Newcastle United in both the Carabao Cup and Premier League – have been achieved without Jack Grealish, who has been suspended by the club following a breach of indiscipline reportedly linked to a missed training session.
 Manager David Moyes confirmed on Thursday that Grealish will again miss out at Hill Dickinson Stadium and in his absence other Everton players have stepped to the fore.
 Striker Thierno Barry scored in both wins against Newcastle to take his tally for this season to eight, already matching his total from 2025-26 despite playing 29 fewer matches.
 Winger Tyrique George, 20, provided the winning assist on Monday at St James' Park, where 19-year-old midfielder Harrison Armstrong was again an influential performer.
 The club's younger players have been growing in influence this season and while Moyes' hand has been partly forced by player departures resulting in a small playing squad, the average age of Everton's starting XI has been the youngest of the Scot's managerial career.
 Everton's youth have been ably supported by an experienced core in recent weeks, with midfielder Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall back close to his best.
 The 28-year-old has created 21 chances in the Premier League this season, more than double the tally of any other Everton player.
 Barry, George and Dewsbury-Hall will all likely be needed if Everton are to continue their winning run against a Coventry side improving steadily in recent weeks.

 One change for Everton as Lampard sticks with Coventry's winning formual published at 18:49 GMT 18:49 GMT 
 Everton v Coventry (20:00 GMT) 
 Nick Mashiter 
BBC Sport football news reporter at the Hill Dickinson Stadium 
 Everton boss David Moyes makes one change to face Coventry.
 Tyler Dibling is in with Jake O'Brien dropping to the bench from Monday's 1-0 win at Newcastle meaning Merlin Rohl will slot in at right-back.
 Everton XI: Pickford, Rohl, Branthwaite, Tarkowski, Mykolenko, Garner, Armstrong, Dibling, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry
 Subs: Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, O'Brien, Johnson, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham
 Coventry are unchanged from their 3-1 win over Sunderland.
 Frank Lampard's side are looking for a fourth win in six Premier League games to put further distance between them and the bottom three.
 Tchaouna replaces Ephron Mason-Clark on the Sky Blues' bench while defender Bobby Thomas is not risked following a calf problem. 
 Coventry XI: Rushworth, Da Silva, Pinnock, Mfuni, Van Ewijk, Torp, Yirenkyi, Sakamoto, Rudoni, Gboho, Awoniyi
 Subs: Bentley, Grimes, Tchaouna Latibeaudiere Kesler-Hayden, Thomas-Asante, Hamer, Simms, Cherif.
